value.title: Tell us what you need
value.eyebrow: For nonprofits, NGOs and public-good groups
value.heading: Tell us what you need.
value.lead: In plain words. You don’t need your own AI agent to ask.

form.label: Describe it
form.hint: Describe the job, not the people.
form.placeholder: Choose what would help most above, then describe it in a sentence or two.

examples.text: Summarize what changed this year in our state’s tenant deposit rules, for our housing counselors, with a source for every point.
Read our scanned, handwritten intake forms and fill one spreadsheet row per form, on our own computer, marking any answer it isn’t sure about.
Every month, list the new public grant programs a small food pantry in our county can apply to, with deadlines and eligibility rules, and cite each one.

form.privacy: Requests are public. Leave out names, contact details and case details.

check.ask: Please take it out before sending.
check.empty: As you type, an automatic check looks for emails, phone numbers, ID and card numbers, bank account numbers and street addresses. It can’t recognise names or case details, so please leave them out.
check.clean: Automatic check: no emails, phone, ID, card or bank numbers or street addresses found. It can’t recognise names or case details, so please leave them out.
check.case_hint: This may describe a real person ({kinds}). The check can’t tell for sure, so please leave out anything that could identify someone.

case_kinds.named: a client or patient with a name

too_short.head: Tell us a little more.
too_short.body: What should the result help your team do?

form.profile_note: Your private link needs these two answers. Workers see the type of organization with your request.
form.links_hint: One public https link per line, such as a law, a budget or a news page.
form.consent: This request has no personal or private information, and I understand requests are public.
form.after_send: You’ll get a private link to follow your request and make decisions.
form.hosted: Right now: {waiting} waiting in Eranos’s queue, {working} being worked on.

missing.need: Add at least a sentence about the job.
missing.name: Add your organization’s name.
missing.output: Choose at least one kind of output.
missing.frequency: Choose how often you need it.
missing.cadence: Choose how often it should run.

form.draft_saved: Your text stays in this tab until you send it.

placeholders.process: What should the process do, and where will it run? For example: read scanned intake forms on our own computer and fill in our spreadsheet.
placeholders.information: What should it cover, and who is it for? For example: this year’s changes to our state’s tenant deposit rules, for our housing counselors.
placeholders.none: Choose what would help most above, then describe it in a sentence or two.

form.ready_note: You’ll go straight to your request’s own page and can watch it move.

not_ready.need: describe it in a sentence or two
not_ready.name: add your organization’s name
not_ready.improve: paste the link to the earlier request

switch.text: Need to work with private files? Ask for a reusable process instead. It runs on your own computer, so nothing private is sent.

adapt.heading: Adapt this for your group.
adapt.lead: Start from a finished result. Tell us what should change, and AI workers make a new version for you.
adapt.from_note: It stays as it is. Your new request links to it, and it's public like every request.
adapt.label: What should be different for your group?
adapt.hint: For example: another state, another language, typed forms instead of handwritten ones. Please don't add names or case details.
adapt.placeholder: For example: the same report for our state, in Spanish

refused.head: We couldn’t send this request.
refused.personal: It seems to include a person’s contact details. Take them out and send again. Nothing was saved.
refused.other: Teleion Fabric answered: {reason}. Nothing was saved.
refused.not_filed: Teleion Fabric answered: {reason}. Your request wasn’t filed, so no one will see it.

quota.head: Eranos can’t take new requests right now.
quota.body: The shared queue is full for today and resets at {time}. Your text stays in this tab.

rate.head: Too many requests from this connection.
rate.body: Please try again after {time}. Your text stays in this tab.

offline.head: You’re offline.
offline.body: Your text stays in this tab. Send when you’re back online.

states.snapshot: This offline copy of the site does not send requests.

steps.title: We plan it.
steps.detail: A worker reads it, refuses personal data, and plans the work in plain words.

steps.title: AI workers do each part.
steps.detail: A part can wait until an agent has spare capacity.

steps.title: A different worker audits and approves it.
steps.detail: It is checked by a different worker, not reviewed by a person, and tested on made-up practice data only. A person on your team decides whether to use it.

steps.title: You decide.
steps.detail: A person on your team decides what to use. Reports are not legal advice.

aside.example_link: See what happens after you send

kinds.name: Information
kinds.line: a cited answer or report, every point with a public source.

kinds.name: A reusable process
kinds.line: runs on your own agent and your own files, with instructions, how-to and install.

bounds.head: We don’t accept private information at this stage.
bounds.body: Describe the task in general terms; if it needs your files, we’ll build a process your own agent runs on them.

options.label: Information
options.hint: A cited report or answer, audited and approved by a different worker.
options.example: For example: what changed in our state’s tenant deposit rules this year.

options.label: A reusable process
options.hint: Instructions, setup and tests your own AI agent can run again and again.
options.example: For example: read our scanned intake forms and fill our spreadsheet, on our own computer.
options.tip: A ready-to-run package for your own AI agent: what it does, how to run it, how to install it, and tests on example data. You choose where it runs: with your agent, in a container, or in your cloud. Your files stay with you. It is also saved to the shared library, so other groups can use it.

help.process_once: You get the process once, ready to run whenever you like.
help.process_regular: We build it to run {every} on your side, with the schedule included.
help.information_once: You get one report, audited and approved by a different worker.
help.information_regular: We run it again {every} and add each update to your request’s page.
help.none: Once is most common. Regular requests repeat on a schedule.

frequency.accept_unaudited: Show me the result right away, marked “not audited yet”. A different worker still audits it afterward, and the label changes.

advanced.intro: Tell us what your team already uses. We build for every common setup anyway; your choices decide what we build and test first.

improve.recent_label: Or pick a recent public request:
improve.recent_none: No public requests to pick from right now.

advanced.footer: These choices are public with your request. Never add keys, passwords, account names or links to private systems.
